post.caption: Gold from mercury made headlines. In July 1924, Berlin professor Adolf Miethe announced gold made from mercury. In his quartz mercury lamp, he reported gold in a sooty film. London's Morning Post ran the headline Gold from Mercury, and Nature's editors said it must be received with great reserve. In Tokyo, Hantaro Nagaoka reported about a milligram of gold. Scientific American sent a duplicate lamp to New York University, and its test was an entire failure to confirm the gold. In 1926, an Oxford physicist said the gold came from the electrodes. The lamp ran on just 170 volts.
